audit_notes: Model: a rigid tile (E = 5 GPa, 0.5 mm; bending stiffness >> foundation) on a soft silicone foundation; under a barnacle pull the tile translates, so the compliance per area is that of the foundation, C = t_f/G_f = 1.5e-3/2e5 = 7.5e-9 m/Pa (linear 1D shear model, analytic w(z) = tau t_f z / G_f). Fouling release (Kendall thin-layer): sigma_c = sqrt(2 w_a / C). Honest trade-off captured by the model: barnacle cement adheres to the hard, higher-energy tile surface with w_a ~ 0.3 J/m2 instead of ~0.05 J/m2 on silicone. Design sigma_c = sqrt(0.6/7.5e-9) = 8.9 kPa vs standard foul-release (0.3 mm, G 0.33 MPa, w_a 0.05) sigma_c = sqrt(0.1/9.1e-10) = 10.5 kPa -> ~15% easier release, much less than a soft thick silicone (the dolphin elite reaches ~4 kPa). Not captured: the tile-rocking peel mechanism when a barnacle spans tile gaps (could improve release further, needs a 4th-order plate-on-foundation model) and edge crack initiation at tile gaps. Drag: tiles flush, gaps 50 um filled; gap Reynolds number w+ ~ 6 and step heights ~5 um (k+ ~ 0.6) make the surface hydraulically smooth, so wall shear equals the smooth baseline within ~0.5%; the concept gives no drag reduction. Durability: hard tiles protect against abrasion and fender loads (main failure mode of soft foul-release), a real advantage; risks are tile debonding by water ingress at gaps and thermal-cycling fatigue of the tile/silicone bond. Dimensionless: t_f/tile_size = 0.5, tile/foundation stiffness ratio E_t/G_f = 2.5e4, gap w+ = 6.2, step k+ = 0.6.

performance_gain.label: Reduction of fouling detachment stress vs standard foul-release coating

baseline_description: Standard clean silicone foul-release coating, 0.3 mm, E ~ 1 MPa, silicone surface
